title: Timelocked credit journeys and upgrade nudges (experiment matrix)
creator: Lina Morales
description: Goal: improve PLG conversion by experimenting with time-locked credit mechanics and contextual upgrade nudges. We will test whether changing how credits expire, how they are revealed to users over time, and which in-product prompts are shown increases paid conversion while preserving developer trust and reducing support load. This ticket owns the experiment matrix, measurement plan, and the first staging rollouts (backend + console + email).
hypothesis: H1: Staggered release of credits (daily micro-allowances) will increase early engagement and lead to higher 14-day conversion vs. a single large upfront credit pool.
H2: Expiry reminders delivered in-product aligned to high-leverage usage (e.g., hitting token thresholds or embedding quota) will convert better than generic expiry emails.
H3: Offering a short-term discount or limited-time burst extension at the moment of opt-out (when credits run out) will convert more enterprise-eligible teams without hurting long-term ARR quality.
H4: Exposing a clear per-feature credit balance (chat vs embeddings) reduces accidental spend and increases trust, improving NPS among trialers.
experiment_matrix: Arm A: One-time 10k token credit, 30-day expiry (control)
Arm B: Daily drip of 330 tokens for 30 days (timelock drip)
Arm C: 10k credit split into pools: 7k for chat, 3k for embeddings; notifications triggered per-pool at 80% remaining
Arm D: 10k credit + automated 3-day pre-expiry in-console banner + behavior-triggered modal with 20% discount offer
Arm E: Controlled cohort with explicit ‘pause auto-join’ checkbox and calendar-scheduled credit reminders (enterprise-friendly)
Cross-experiment: Email cadence variation (2-day pre-expiry vs 1-day vs none) combined orthogonally with Arms B/C/D
primary_metrics: Retention of activated seats (teams with >1 active developer in first 30 days)
secondary_metrics: Average tokens used per active day
Support ticket volume related to credit confusion
segmentation: New orgs vs returning orgs (previously signed up but inactive)
Use-case buckets: chat prototyping vs vector-search/embeddings
Region (NA, EMEA, APAC) to understand differences in upgrade behavior
implementation_notes: Backend: feature flag gated credit scheduling service (reuse existing credit ledger schema; add 'timelock_schedule' enum)
Console: new credit UI component showing per-pool balances, expiry timer, and CTA for upgrade/extend
Email: templated pre-expiry and expiry emails with experiment token for attribution
Telemetry: assign experiment id and exposure events (arm-assigned, drip-delivered, reminder-shown, CTA-clicked)
Safety: automatic rollback if product analytics show >10% spike in support tickets or >15% negative NPS shift in 7 days
data_and_analysis: Primary analysis in Amplitude and Looker for conversion cohorts; create a dedicated dashboard comparing arms side-by-side
Survival analysis to measure the shape of conversion over time (time-to-convert), not just final conversion
Instrument incremental impact (ATE) with bootstrapped confidence intervals; pre-register analysis plan
Track enterprise signal (contact-sales form or security questionnaire request) as a leading indicator for high-value conversions
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Drip design could frustrate power users who expect bulk credits. Mitigation: provide toggle in onboarding to switch to bulk credit for experienced users.
Risk: Discount modal harms perception of list pricing. Mitigation: limit to first 2% of cohorts and use timebox to measure lift before wider rollout.
Risk: Complexity increases support cost. Mitigation: ship clear in-console help text and a KB article; route edge cases to SE queue for hands-on follow up.
Risk: Enterprise procurement friction for timelocked credits (legal asks). Mitigation: signal to sales when org reaches 100k tokens consumed in trial to proactively offer contract path.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment implemented behind a feature flag and deployable to staging
Instrumentation emits exposure and outcome events with experiment id and arm
Console UI surfaces per-pool balances and the drip visualization for Arm B
Email templates created and linked to campaign tracking parameters
Dashboard in Looker/Amplitude comparing arms loaded and accessible to PM/Eng/Design
dependencies: OPS-78 (email campaign infra for transactional experiments)
